connectedApps.title: Connected apps
connectedApps.noneTitle: No connected apps are set up on this server
connectedApps.noneBody: The server administrator turns each app on. Until then, nothing here can be connected.
connectedApps.linkCard: Slack alerts, your Google Calendar, Google Drive and Salesforce.
connectedApps.slack.title: Slack alerts
connectedApps.slack.sub: A short message in one channel when something happens. The GMS posts and lists public channels; it never reads messages.
connectedApps.slack.channelHelp: A public channel. Private channels and direct messages are not used.
connectedApps.slack.inviteBody: Slack takes messages only from apps in the channel. Add the app to the channel in Slack, then save here.
connectedApps.slack.whatIsSent: Each message names the event and the record, with a link. It never includes an applicant's answers, email addresses or amounts.
connectedApps.calendar.title: My Google Calendar
connectedApps.calendar.subFunder: Your workspace's opportunity deadlines, written to a calendar of yours as all-day events.
connectedApps.calendar.subApplicant: Your application deadlines and report due dates, written to a calendar of yours as all-day events.
connectedApps.calendar.yours: This is your own calendar. Each person on the team connects their own.
connectedApps.calendar.whichHelp: One you own. Events are written only there.
connectedApps.calendar.written: {count, plural, =0 {No deadlines to write yet.} one {# deadline written.} other {# deadlines written.}}
connectedApps.calendar.status: {count, plural, =0 {No deadlines} one {# deadline} other {# deadlines}} in {calendar}
connectedApps.calendar.what: Updated every hour. Each event has a title, a date and a link: no guests, no video call, no emails.
connectedApps.drive.sub: Attach files from Google Drive and save as-submitted copies to it. The GMS sees only the files you choose.
connectedApps.salesforce.sub: Import records from Salesforce, read only. The GMS never changes anything in Salesforce.
driveAttach.failed: The file could not be copied from Google Drive.
driveAttach.saveToDrive: Save the as-submitted copy to Google Drive
salesforcePick.sourceHelp: Read grants or accounts, or a query of your own. The GMS only reads from Salesforce.
salesforcePick.youSignIn: You sign in with Salesforce. The GMS only runs read queries and never changes a record.
salesforcePick.heading: What should be read from Salesforce?
salesforcePick.chooseWhatToRead: Choose what to read from Salesforce.
salesforcePick.readOnly: Read only: one query, at most 5,000 records each time.
salesforcePick.grantsHelp: Opportunities with a grant record type, as the Nonprofit Success Pack keeps them.
salesforcePick.accountsHelp: Organizations: name, type, website and location.
salesforcePick.soqlHelp: Start with SELECT. Queries that change or lock records are refused.
awardKit.federal.title: Federal funding
awardKit.federal.paidWithFederalMoney: This award is paid in whole or in part with federal money
awardKit.federal.percent: Federal share of the project’s total costs (%)
awardKit.federal.agencyHelp: As it should read in the statement, for example: the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
awardKit.federal.onlyWithBoth: The share kit adds the statement of the federal share of costs only when both the amount and the percentage are entered. Nothing is worked out for you.
awardKit.federal.notSaved: The federal funding was not saved.
awardKit.federal.noStatementYet: Enter both the federal amount and the percentage to add the statement to the share kit.
awardKit.federal.summary: Federally funded: {amount}, {percent}% of the project’s total costs.
awardKit.federal.markedNoNumbers: Marked as federally funded. The funder has not entered both numbers yet.
awardKit.federal.statementDetail: Federal rules ask for this statement in press releases, publications and other public statements about the project. When other funders pay part of the costs, add the dollar amount and percentage paid by non-governmental sources too.
awardKit.downloadFailed: The file could not be made.
awardKit.portrait.title: Portrait card
awardKit.portrait.detail: 1080 × 1350, for Instagram and LinkedIn: both organizations’ names and the program, with no logos.
awardKit.portrait.showAmount: Show the amount on the card
awardKit.portrait.amountHidden: The funder hides award amounts, so the card shows none
awardKit.carousel.title: Carousel (PDF)
awardKit.carousel.detail: {count, plural, one {# slide} other {# slides}} of 1080 × 1350, for a LinkedIn document post. Add each slide’s alt text where you post it.
awardKit.carousel.whatAlt: the alt text for each slide
awardKit.press.title: Press release
awardKit.press.detail: Ready to edit. Fill in the parts in brackets. It credits the funder as “{credit}”.
awardKit.tag.title: Page to tag
awardKit.tag.none: {name} has not shared a page to tag.
awardKit.settings.title: Share-kit settings
awardKit.settings.detail: Your social page, and whether others may tag it when they post about grants you are part of. Only your workspace’s admins change these.
awardKit.settings.adminsChange: Only your workspace’s admins change these settings.
awardKit.settings.pageHelp: The https address of your page on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X, Bluesky or Threads. A new address needs your consent again.
awardKit.settings.consentGrantee: Funders may tag this page when they post about our grants
awardKit.settings.consentFunder: Grantees may tag this page when they post about our grants
awardKit.settings.credit: How the press release credits you
awardKit.settings.descriptionHelp: Used for “About” in press releases and on the carousel. Without it, the mission on your public page is used.
